title: God ordinarily prepares by preventing grace
source_text: XVI. Verum quamvis nullus ex se ad veram justitiam & sanctitatem pervenire, aut ad eam sese disponere possit; sed necesse sit illam a Deo modo quodam naturam superante in animam infundi, non solet tamen Deus justitiam istam in anima creare, & homines Spiritu sanctificante donare, quin prius ipse illos ad hoc disponat & prae-paret quibusdam actibus atque affectibus intus in animis eorum excitatis, vi & au-xilio gratiae illius qua Deus homines a se alienos, & adhuc mortuos in peccatis prae-venit.
pass_a_gloss: But although no one of himself can arrive at true righteousness and holiness, or dispose himself for it, but it must be infused into the soul by God in a manner surpassing nature, yet God is not accustomed to create that righteousness in the soul and to endow men with the sanctifying Spirit without first himself disposing and preparing them for this by certain acts and affections inwardly excited in their minds by the force and help of that grace by which God prevents men alienated from him and still dead in sins.
pass_b_english: Though none can reach or dispose himself to true holiness unaided, God ordinarily first prepares by preventing grace.
He excites inward acts and affections before creating that justice in the soul.

choices.why: Key lemma for De Justitia densify §1050.
